name: Isolated Pyloric Duplication

criteria.description: Presence of a cystic or tubular structure contiguous with the pyloric region of the stomach
Duplication cyst wall containing smooth muscle layers similar to normal pyloric musculature
Inner lining of the duplication cyst composed of gastrointestinal mucosa, often gastric-type epithelium
Radiologic or ultrasonographic identification of cystic lesion adjacent to pylorus

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Identification of a cystic structure contiguous with the pylorus demonstrating smooth muscle wall and gastrointestinal mucosal lining
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is typically confirmed by histopathological examination after surgical excision.

searchTerms: projectile vomiting with clear stomach contents
palpable lump in upper middle abdomen
poor feeding with feeling full quickly
difficulty eating due to early satiety

common.symptomName: Intermittent abdominal pain localized to upper abdomen

occasional.symptomName: Gastrointestinal bleeding due to mucosal ulceration
searchTerms: bleeding in digestive tract from ulcers
gastrointestinal bleeding caused by mucosal sores
blood loss due to stomach or intestinal ulcers
loss of body fluids due to vomiting

rare.symptomName: Infection or abscess formation within cyst

laboratory: Mild electrolyte imbalances secondary to vomiting
imaging: Ultrasound showing cystic lesion adjacent to pylorus with double wall sign
Upper gastrointestinal contrast study demonstrating extrinsic mass effect on pyloric channel
CT or MRI confirming cystic duplication with characteristic wall layers
genetic: No known genetic mutations specifically associated
other: Histopathology confirming smooth muscle wall and gastrointestinal mucosal lining

distinguishingFeatures: Thickened pyloric muscle without cystic duplication
No separate cystic structure on imaging
Typically presents with projectile vomiting but no palpable cystic mass
Duplication cyst located in gastric body or fundus rather than pylorus
May have different symptom profile depending on location

redFlags: Persistent non-bilious projectile vomiting in neonate
Palpable abdominal mass in epigastric region
Signs of dehydration or electrolyte imbalance
references: Surgical Pathology Clinics. Gastrointestinal Duplication Cysts: A Review. 2020.
Journal of Pediatric Surgery. Clinical Features and Management of Pyloric Duplication Cysts. 2018.
